main_text.p: hoc seu quotus ille in 3 diuisorem multiplicatus, efficit 9, qui eo loci 900 ualet, tria nempe solida D simul sumpta. Porrò idem quotus quadratè multiplicatus erit 9, qui post in triplum ductus, facit 27, quae eo loci 270 ualent, triplum Parallelepipedum minus C simul sumptum. Demum idem quotus cubicè multiplicatus, parit cubum B. Factis igitur hisce tribus additis, & à suprapositis deductis, nihil restat, quod designat Cubum fuisse datum numerum. Exemplum est ut uides:

Res pluribus exemplis explicetur. Sit dati Cubi 16387064, latus inueniendum: hunc igitur punctis in periodos quasdam digere. Ac primùm latus cubi sub ultimo numero inuenti inquire. Verùm cum 16 cubus nō sit, cubi proximè minoris, nempe 8, latus 2 in quotū adnota, cubumq; deduc à 16, restant 8. Atq; hoc primum opus ad reliqua deinceps puncta non iterabitur, sequentibus praeceptis toties semper repetitis, quot puncta superfuerint. Prima inductio sic est:

page.notes: The arithmetic (the long division and the parallelepiped and cube workings) is set in a column of small figures and has been transcribed line by line as far as legible; alignment and some digits (e.g. the cube root rows, the figures after "1000") are approximate. The printed superscript signs in the division are not reproduced exactly. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The right edge strip shows the neighbouring page and is omitted.
